summary.headline: Ador Welding Q4 FY26: revenue up ~3% YoY, EBITDA ~INR38 crore (+200 bps), with management guiding to 100–200 bps further EBITDA margin gains.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 revenue growth of about 3% YoY, EBITDA of about INR38 crore (up 200 bps) and gross margin of about 36%, excluding the Kuwait recovery and exceptional items. For FY26, standalone revenue grew about 2%, gross margin rose about 250 bps to 38%, and the Kuwait recovery of INR14 crore lifted PBT to about INR130 crore excluding the Uran onerous cost. The Flares and Process Equipment division has been folded into a single welding segment, with loss-making large projects being wound down in favour of product-line business. Management declined to give formal guidance, but flagged Middle East dispatch disruption in March, a Saudi market that is now the third-largest export market, and a longer-term aspiration to triple earnings.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 PBT (excl. Kuwait recovery and exceptionals)

financial_highlights.change: recovery of 2020-21 receivables, booked as impairment reversal

segments.name: Welding (consumables, equipment, MNR)
segments.commentary: Now the only reported segment after the Flares and Process Equipment division was merged in. Management says welding is growing roughly in line with steel consumption and that domestic India is about 80%+ of sales. Consumables and equipment are said to grow in similar cycles, with equipment spiking during capex upcycles.

segments.name: Flares and Process Equipment (PE)
segments.commentary: Folded into the welding business effective around end-March 2026 and run as product lines of INR20-30 crore. Management says there is no further loss, and that the Uran project is about 96-97% complete. The Q4 result included a INR3 crore gain from an ONGC reorder.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance, but expects EBITDA margin to improve by a further 100-200 bps over coming periods, partly via gross margin, and sees it as feasible within FY27 barring severe supply shocks.
Aspirational target: revenue of INR2,000 crore by FY29 (roughly 25% CAGR) is still referenced, but management says the main principle is to triple earnings over the period.
Management's planning assumption is growth at least in line with IIP/GDP (6-8%), and it believes it can outperform that.
Capex is guided at about INR30-35 crore for FY27 (maintenance INR10-12 crore; two to three new consumable lines), possibly up to INR40 crore a year over the next two years.

Management says it would be feasible to reach INR1,500-1,600 crore of welding revenue by FY28 only if the economy stays strong, which implies about 18-20% growth a year; it has not committed to that figure.
Exports were flattish in FY26 (last year's total cited as about INR154 crore), with a better outlook from order book and approvals.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation is about 70% on a fair estimate, with some lines running at 90-95% and needing capex.
Normal sustainable operating range is cited as 70-90% depending on equipment age and technology.
Two to three new consumable lines are due this year and next, all in welding consumables rather than equipment.
Capex needed to double volume over five to seven years is estimated at INR100-150 crore (plant and machinery, excluding land).
demand_pricing: Demand is described as okay since November-December 2025, but customers are cautious because of inflation in steel and macro conditions.
Around 80-85% of sales go through distributors, so the order book is short-cycle and not a long backlog.

Middle East: March quarter dispatches were hit in the first three to four weeks by the situation there. Most of the pent-up volume was cleared by the end of the quarter, and management says demand remains good.
Saudi Arabia is now the third-largest export market (it was second last year), and inquiries from there have been healthier since December 2025.
Market share is put at about 17-18%, plus or minus a few percent.
Shipbuilding: management says it has approvals for about 75-80% of the required work, but it has not disclosed the revenue from that sector.
Management says it is seeing its best-ever welding automation order book, though the base is still small.
Steel: pricing and inflation are challenging, but management says the cycle is on a brighter footing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are process equipment losses continuing after one-off adjustments, and where does that finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no further negative. The INR3 crore Q4 gain came from an ONGC reorder, the FY26 hit was about INR25 crore, and the division has been restructured into product lines of INR20-30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% EBITDA margin sustainable, and what is the medium-term growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management treats ~12% as the base and aims for incremental, step-by-step improvement. It declined to share internal targets and gave no guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to INR1,500-1,600 crore of welding revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: That would need about 18-20% YoY growth for two years. Management says it is feasible if the economy stays strong, but it would not commit to a number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and were dispatches affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure is high for exports, but management says receivables are secure and demand is firm. March dispatches were hit in the first three to four weeks, and most of the backlog has since cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR30-35 crore, with INR10-12 crore of maintenance. Two to three new consumable lines are coming, with the spend all in welding consumables.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company open to acquisitions, and what is the cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to acquisitions that are more targeted, focused on technology as well as market share. It has not announced any transaction and says the company has a healthy cash balance.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption to dispatches and supply, despite stated strong demand and secure distributor terms.
Steel and supply-chain inflation, which is making customers cautious on orders.
Uran project still at about 96-97% completion with commissioning delays, and a possible further ONGC recovery or LD impact.
Pending Indian income tax demand of about INR14 crore, under appeal; BIS magistrate court proceedings listed for June-July 2026.
Management's growth aspirations (INR2,000 crore by FY29; tripling earnings) are not backed by specific guidance.
Export volumes flat in FY26, and the company is reporting only one segment going forward, so less visibility on the breakdown.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the clean-up of legacy issues, but cautious and often evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give guidance, targets, segment revenue or product-level breakdowns. It was most direct on the completed restructuring and Uran/Kuwait closure.
key_quotes: There is no further loss, there is a gain.
There is no further negative left. We took the biggest hit we did in Q1 and we are working towards recovery on what we can.
So far this year, what we have seen is the order book, inquiry base, and approvals where we are set up, exports should do better -- should do well, should do better for the markets we operate in.
We don't like to give guidance, but that is the way we look at it.

adds.what: 2-3 new welding consumable lines (due this year and next; capex INR30-35 crore for FY27, up to INR40 crore/yr for next two years)

growth.why: Management gives no formal revenue guidance; planning assumption is growth of 6-8% (in line with IIP/GDP, aiming to outperform), backed partly by 2-3 consumable lines due within about two years and FY27 capex of INR30-35 crore, with EBITDA margin up a further 100-200 bps over coming periods, mainly via gross margin.
